ready.title: The test tier-folder sweep removes a finished run lock file only when that run folder is gone, so a folder it could not remove is tried again by a later sweep (the architect O2 at PR 326; filler entry 19)
ready.summary: PLACED S3 2026-11-16 as filler entry 19, after the current entries, by the advisor's ruling ADV-2026-11-16-02 (state/directives/2026-11-16-advisor-ruling-adv-2026-11-16-02-lod-tier-test-sweep-keeps-lock-until-folder-removed-filler-19-s3-budget-30-the-sweep-alone.md), budget 30, the engine lane, no dependency. The finding stands: the sweep removes a finished run's folder and then its lock file, ignoring the first removal's result, so a folder it could not remove loses its lock file and no later sweep finds it again; nothing reaches the machine-wide tier folder (item 1). It changes the sweep in engine/tests/common/mod.rs and nothing else: the lock file of a finished run is removed only when that run's folder is gone, removed by this sweep or already absent; otherwise the lock file stays, and a later sweep tries again (item 3). No file under engine/src or kernel/src changes, and no existing test's assertion (item 3 (a)). The form says how the change is proved: a test needs a folder that cannot be removed while its lock can be opened, for example a file inside it held open by the test; if no test without a timing window can do that, the form gives the mutation and the read that stand in its place, an OPEN item to the advisor (item 3 (b)). The rare lock race at a reused process id is not part of the node; it stays recorded in both gates' reports (item 3 (c)). Ordinary form and gating; rule (00) at the form's commit; its heavy runs yield to PR B's agents (ADV-2026-11-15-17 item 4). Nothing needs the human (item 5). From the architect gate of PR 326, its O2.
